goal: Make checkRouterResponse in src/delivery/asgi-core-profile.mjs reject a router response header name that is empty, upper-case, whitespace-bearing, colon-bearing, or control-character-bearing, throwing the existing TypeError before toResponseEvents ever builds outgoing ASGI response events or call/callFromReceive ever invoke send(). V14Q closed this gap on the inbound (request) header-name path; the outgoing router-response header-name path was still unguarded: any object key, however malformed, was silently lower-cased and placed into the outgoing http.response.start header pairs.
nonGoals: no new dependency, listener, HTTP/net/fs capability, environment read, clock or randomness use
no restriction of valid existing lower-case response header names
no change to request header decoding, method, path, or response body/status handling

scopeResolution.note: Minimal production fix: checkRouterResponse now checks every string-keyed own key of response.headers with isValidHeaderName(key), the same RFC 7230 token-class-restricted-to-lower-case predicate decodeHeaders already uses for inbound request headers (HEADER_NAME_TOKEN_PATTERN = /^[a-z0-9!#$%&'*+\-.^_`|~]+$/). A key that is empty, upper-case, whitespace-bearing, colon-bearing, or control-character-bearing fails the check and checkRouterResponse throws the same TypeError it already throws for other malformed router-response shapes, before toResponseEvents lower-cases/sorts any header pair and before call/callFromReceive ever call send(). Because a valid name is already lower-case by construction, the existing name.toLowerCase() in toResponseEvents becomes a no-op for accepted names and is left untouched to keep the diff minimal. No router, request-header, method, path, status, or body logic touched.

red.note: Added a dedicated handle test asserting a battery of malformed router response header names (empty, upper-case, spaces, embedded colon, newline, tab, carriage return) each throw TypeError from handle; a companion call test asserting the same TypeError is thrown before send() is ever invoked; and a companion test asserting valid lower-case token response header names, including the full RFC 7230 token separator set, still dispatch and appear correctly sorted in the outgoing http.response.start headers. Also normalized the two pre-existing tests that used mixed-case router response header names (Content-Type/X-Request-Id, Mid) to their lower-case equivalents, since those shapes are no longer valid router output under this conformance rule. Against the pre-fix source, the malformed-name cases all failed: checkRouterResponse accepted every header key unchecked, so toResponseEvents silently lower-cased and emitted the malformed name instead of throwing.

green.results: All 47 tests pass, including the new response-header-name-token assertions and every pre-existing scope/method/request-header/response/encoder assertion. npm run check exits GREEN with no new failures.

acceptance.emptyResponseHeaderNameRejected: a router response header name of '' throws TypeError from handle/call before any event is built or sent
acceptance.upperCaseResponseHeaderNameRejected: a router response header name such as 'Content-Type' or 'CONTENT-TYPE' throws TypeError from handle/call before any event is built or sent
acceptance.whitespaceResponseHeaderNameRejected: a router response header name containing a space, leading/trailing space, or embedded colon throws TypeError from handle/call before any event is built or sent
acceptance.controlCharResponseHeaderNameRejected: a router response header name containing \n, \t, or \r throws TypeError from handle/call before any event is built or sent
acceptance.callDoesNotInvokeSendOnRejection: call rejects with TypeError and send is never invoked when the router response carries a malformed header name
acceptance.validLowerCaseTokenNamesUnaffected: valid lower-case HTTP token response header names, including the full RFC 7230 token separator character set, continue to be emitted and sorted deterministically in http.response.start exactly as before

rollback.trigger: the added response-header-name-token check is found to reject a legitimate header name shape, or any existing test regresses
rollback.action: revert the isValidHeaderName(key) loop added to checkRouterResponse in src/delivery/asgi-core-profile.mjs, and the added/normalized tests, this planning file and the CHANGELOG entry, as one shard
rollback.blastRadius: one function (checkRouterResponse) inside src/delivery/asgi-core-profile.mjs; no other function or file touched
rollback.runtimeDataImpact: none; no runtime, DB, or I/O surface involved

capabilityDelta: ASGI_RESPONSE_HEADER_NAME_CONFORMANCE: a router response header name that is empty, upper-case, whitespace-bearing, colon-bearing, or control-character-bearing now throws TypeError from checkRouterResponse before an outgoing ASGI response event is built or sent, instead of being silently lower-cased and emitted onto the wire-facing http.response.start event.

userJourney.once: asgi-core-profile.mjs, checkRouterResponse sadece response.headers'ın sıradan bir obje olup olmadığına bakıyordu; router'ın döndürdüğü 'Content-Type' gibi büyük harfli veya boşluk/iki nokta/kontrol karakteri taşıyan bozuk bir header adı, hiç doğrulanmadan küçük harfe çevrilip giden http.response.start olayına ekleniyordu.
userJourney.simdi: checkRouterResponse artık router yanıtındaki her header adının geçerli bir küçük harfli HTTP token'ı olmasını şart koşuyor; boş, büyük harfli, boşluklu, iki nokta taşıyan veya kontrol karakteri taşıyan bir ad, olay hiç oluşturulmadan veya send() hiç çağrılmadan TypeError ile reddediliyor.
userJourney.fark: src/delivery/asgi-core-profile.mjs içinde checkRouterResponse'a, decodeHeaders'ın istek tarafında zaten kullandığı aynı header-adı-token doğrulama yardımcı fonksiyonuyla bir kontrol döngüsü eklendi. Geçerli küçük harfli response header adlarının davranışı ve sıralı deterministik çıktısı hiç değişmedi.
userJourney.kullaniciYolculugu: Router çağıran koddaki bir hata nedeniyle bozuk biçimli bir yanıt header adı (örn. büyük harf, boşluk, iki nokta veya kontrol karakteri taşıyan) üretirse, artık bu bozuk ad host adaptörüne hiç ulaşmadan, giden olay hiç kurulmadan TypeError ile durduruluyor. Bu paket bir sunucu/host seçmiyor; sadece mevcut çağrılabilir fonksiyonun giden header doğrulamasını sıkılaştırıyor.
userJourney.kalanEngel: Hâlâ gerçek bir HTTP sunucusu/host adaptörü bu callable'ı sarmalamıyor; bu yüzden runnableProduct hâlâ false.
